provenance.dataset: temp/agent_tuning, seeds 4200/4201, T50/T100/T300, M10/M90; algorithm seed 0
provenance.kind: 96 paired fixed-control probes on 12 development states after a common 300-trial prefix; not real Agent performance
provenance.caveat: State probes reset RNG. Nested starts are dependent; these observations do not prove full-run superiority or isolate individual knobs.
provenance.acceptance_probes: 48 paired 200-trial probes on all eight residual T300 final development states; spatial30/global/best-only and RNG0 held fixed; only acceptance changed.
provenance.large_run_observations: Nine complete T300 development runs, seeds5200-5202, M10/M50/M90, algorithm seed0; no formal outcomes.
provenance.neighborhood_comparison: Nine full T300 runs on the same development seeds; aggregate L1=55 versus 62 in the reference runs; no formal feedback.

scope: Single Agent, random selectors, zero features. Illustrations are hypotheses, never forced schedules.

initial.lesson: The example is an initial hypothesis, not measured initial-state superiority: the paired probes begin after a common prefix. Start with a compact best-only repair hypothesis and moderate destruction unless live evidence supports alternatives. Both selectors remain random. Focus can be tested for scarce insertion opportunities; it need not be permanently active. High-maturity starts have much useful structure already: use the live gap and actual removal counts. Do not assume the entire action should use a large-backlog strategy.

rationale.reason: Test this complete neighborhood when supported by live state and history; keep random task choice separate from best-position repair.

stalled.lesson: If residual service stalls, inspect actual complete controls and distinguish energy-only progress from task recovery. Consider changing the leading spatial/time/random family or removal intensity. Focus cannot remove assigned blockers. Best-only repair is a useful starting hypothesis; random position repair may disrupt feasible structure. Best-only repair is a hypothesis, not a permanent restriction. If the same service gap persists despite changing removal/acceptance with best-only repair, testing mixed best+random POSITION repair is another legal neighborhood; random task selection alone cannot test a different insertion position. Recorded sparse-start success motivates this alternative but is not measured residual-state superiority. Do not keep quoting a failed example as if it were untried.

rationale.reason: Probe a small energy barrier crossing at equal service when the live acceptance counts and residual stagnation support it; keep the measured spatial/best-only neighborhood and compare the outcome.

stalled.measured_contrast: On all nine residual states, spatial30/global versus mixed20/global gave 5 wins, 4 ties, 0 losses in the full lexicographic objective; both used best-only repair. spatial20 gave 3/3/3; focus20 3/4/2; worst20 0/6/3; anneal20 1/5/3. The entire spatial30 control is an evidence-backed alternative after mixed destruction stalls, not a guaranteed schedule. Do not add random-position repair and describe it as the tested control.
stalled.observational_failure: The first real Agent candidate selected best+random position repair in all 144 actions. Its twelve development runs left total missed priority 68. This is an observed failure pattern, not a causal repair ablation.
stalled.acceptance_contrast: Compared with greedy at the same residual state, tolerant .02, .05 and .10 each gave 4 wins, 2 ties, 2 losses in full objective across eight T300 states. SA .02 and .05 each gave 3/1/4. Thus test tolerant .02 or .05 when energy rejection blocks a service-stalled promising neighborhood; larger tolerance is not proven superior. These paired probes reset RNG and adaptive history; they are not full Agent performance evidence.

progress.lesson: A service-improving complete control can be continued. Do not abandon it just because exact-vector counts reset. If service improvement stops, compare newer residual evidence rather than cumulative early backlog gains.

energy.lesson: All tasks are assigned, but energy is not proven optimal. Use best-insertion to find low incremental transfer cost. Try worst-cost/spatial or random destruction with moderate removal, retaining full feasibility. Continue controls that reduce energy at equal service. After repeated stagnation and rejected structural changes, a small bounded energy tolerance may open alternatives; never sacrifice service.

rationale.reason: Test this complete neighborhood when supported by live state and history; keep random task choice separate from best-position repair.

energy.measured_contrast: Only three probe states had complete service: spatial20, spatial30, mixed30, time20, worst20 and anneal20 each gave 1 win and 2 ties against mixed20; focus20 tied all three. Evidence is too small to rank these six. Start with best-only positions; use live energy gains to continue, and test a new neighborhood when progress stops.

sparse_initial.state: No current-run history; at most 15 percent of tasks remain unassigned.
sparse_initial.lesson: A nearly populated start can call for a different complete neighborhood than a large backlog. In six actual M90 development runs, the spatial/mixed-position strategy completed 5/6 instances with spatial/worst/random destruction and best+random position repair prominent; the best-only strategy completed 3/6 with mixed best-only initial controls. Total missed priority was 1 versus 4. These whole-run strategies differ in several decisions, so this does NOT isolate repair or prove superiority. Use the illustrated spatial/mixed-position control as a sparse-start hypothesis, retaining random task selection and strict service protection; test the resulting outcome. Best-only remains available, especially after complete coverage for energy refinement.

rationale.reason: Test the observed sparse-start spatial neighborhood and mixed position repair while preserving service. This whole-control example is not causal proof; inspect the resulting coverage.

large_stalled.state: Large residual assignment with at least two consecutive windows without a service improvement.
large_stalled.observed_failure: In the T300/s5201/M10 development run, service stayed at (14,8) from trial500 through1200. Seven further windows used ratio .30, including changes of focus and destroy order, while energy fell. In T300/s5202/M90, a one-task gap persisted through800 although energy improved in every window. These are trajectories, not controlled attribution.
large_stalled.lesson: Do not count energy refinement as task recovery. Compare the actual service-gap history. If small neighborhoods and focus changes were already unsuccessful, test a wider removal size while preserving a plausible family and repair policy. Ratios .40/.50 are legal and mean at most40/50 removals, not40/50 percent of300 tasks. The illustrated .50 control is a NEW hypothesis motivated by untested intensity, not a measured winner. If that size already failed or destroyed most useful structure, compare a different leading family or insertion-position mix using live evidence. Energy tolerance only helps energy barriers, never rejected service losses.

rationale.reason: Test a wider destruction neighborhood when the same service gap survived the observed smaller neighborhoods; this is an unmeasured hypothesis, and the next window must decide whether to continue.

large_initial.state: Large instance with substantial unassigned backlog and no current-run control history.
large_initial.lesson: Consider a spatially coherent neighborhood with moderate-wide destruction and best-position repair. At the start there are no rejection observations: energy tolerance is a hypothesis, not a measured barrier. Preserve the service prefix and judge the next window. Use actual removal counts and available budget rather than maturity labels.
large_initial.development_basis: In T300/s5202/M10, the spatial/random/time family with best-only repair, ratios .40/.50 and tolerant .02 reduced the service gap from (14,8) at600 to (5,3) at1200. In s5200/M50 this wider family failed to resolve (12,7). These are complete-control trajectories; transferring this neighborhood to an initial state is UNMEASURED, not a causal result or a compulsory policy.

rationale.reason: Test a spatial neighborhood with best-position repair and bounded energy exploration for the current large backlog; validate service recovery before continuing.

large_rebuild.state: At least three service-stalled windows on a large residual state, including an observed ratio .40 or larger.
large_rebuild.lesson: Further widening or focus oscillation may revisit the same repair basin. Check which insertion POSITION policies were actually tried at this service gap. If every failed neighborhood used only best_insertion, consider a bounded mixed best/random-position window with moderate destruction; the random task selector does not provide this position diversity. This is a hypothesis: if mixed positions already failed at this gap, prefer another control supported by current evidence. Retain earlier failures, service protection and the global best. Continue only if subsequent outcomes justify it.
large_rebuild.development_basis: s5201/M10 stayed (14,8) from500 to1200 despite wider .40/.50 best-only neighborhoods; s5202/M90 stayed (1,1) to1200 after trying wider best-only repair. The original sparse-start mixed-position example is whole-run evidence, not a measured residual-state advantage.

rationale.reason: Test insertion-position diversity after the recorded wider best-only neighborhoods repeatedly failed at the same service gap. This changes repair behavior without changing random task selection.
